Title: 'It's just as good as class, if not better!'
NewsSummary: One of our medical college students shares his thoughts on learning from home.
NewsContent:
Usman Ansari, a first year MBBS student, is one of many students who are now studying at home using the University's e-learning resources that involve a combination of software to make learning fun and engaging. Here's what Usman has to say about the University's online learning platform:

"When I received news that AKU will be closed due to the COVID-19 outbreak, I was completely stressed out! I was worried about how I would cope with the coursework and the notion of attending online lectures sounded far-fetched and boring.

Three weeks later, my schedule hasn't changed. Our online classes are following the same timetable as our actual sessions at the University and it gives a sense of sanity to have a routine amid all the lockdown chaos around us.

We use Microsoft Teams for online lectures, have our regular class at 8:30 am and continue taking classes throughout the day as if student life has never changed. The video lecture recording, slides and assignments are uploaded on our Moodle Virtual Learning portal promptly and we can easily access them.

For problem-based learning that involves group tasks, we have an online session of 10 students at a time where we are graded on our participation. For lab work in subjects such as pathology, physiology and pharmacology, an instructor conducts the experiments/tasks while we observe via a video conference.

One major advantage of the e-learning option is that students who are shy in a classroom setting also get a chance to ask questions comfortably in chats during the class or after class via email. The teachers are very patient and answer us till we actually feel like we have understood the concepts. Just yesterday I had a query and I emailed my biochemistry faculty and he responded within 10 minutes! Now I feel that e-learning is more efficient: it gives each student more individual attention and we save a lot of time that we can dedicate to studying."

Online classes are currently being offered to Year 1 and 2 MBBS students and will be offered to years 3, 4 and 5 in the near future.
